Threat.value: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Mistrust: People can't be trusted
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening illness trauma, a global appraisal that 'People can't be trusted' is not impossible, but it is hard to justify from the rest of this profile because there are no interpersonal trauma, betrayal, or healthcare-specific trigger/memory items that would support pervasive mistrust. It sits awkwardly with the otherwise illness/body-focused threat and memory pattern.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Injustice: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it
issues.explanation: 'What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it' can fit illness trauma if linked to perceived medical neglect or lack of treatment, but this profile contains no corroborating healthcare-related triggers, memories, or threats. As written, it implies an unresolved external injustice theme that is not reflected elsewhere in the selected items.

issues.item: Injustice: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it
issues.explanation: For a 79-year-old woman whose index trauma is life-threatening illness, these appraisals are the least coherent with the rest of the profile. The other nodes emphasize bodily alarm, confined/proximity triggers, and intrusive sensory memories, which fit illness-related trauma. By contrast, 'nothing has been done about it' and broad interpersonal mistrust imply a human-perpetrated or neglected-by-others trauma context that is not otherwise represented in the triggers, memory, or threat items. While unfairness can follow illness, this specific pair pulls the profile toward betrayal/abuse or institutional wrongdoing in a way that is hard to reconcile with the stated trauma type and the rest of the selected items.

For a 79-year-old woman whose index trauma is life-threatening illness, the appraisal 'People can't be trusted' is the only clearly incoherent item. The rest of the profile is strongly body/illness-centered: confined or close-proximity triggers plausibly map to medical settings, threat items are somatic hyperarousal/false alarm responses, memory items reflect intrusive and fragmented recollection of frightening illness-related experiences, and appraisals about lost capability and an unreliable body fit this trauma well. By contrast, global interpersonal mistrust is more characteristic of interpersonal trauma and is not supported by the trigger, memory, or threat content here. Given the strong Triggers ↔ Negative Appraisals linkage in the formulation, appraisals should plausibly arise from the same trauma network; this item points to a different trauma meaning structure and is hard to explain from the rest of the selected items.
